summary: Preinstall dropper fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload
details: On npm install, package.json's preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime v1.3.13 from GitHub releases (oven-sh/bun), extracts the platform-appropriate `bun` binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-only module (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header) built as a rotating string-array with hex-obfuscated identifiers — the string-array-rotator obfuscation shape — so its behavior is not visible without decoding. setup.mjs itself is additionally obfuscated with `_0x...` hex-suffixed identifiers and per-function string-lookup tables that hide simple flow (Alpine/musl detection, HTTPS download from GitHub, ZIP extract via `unzip`/PowerShell Expand-Archive, chmod, execFileSync). The advertised purpose is a wrapper around Bandwidth Voice BXML steps; nothing in that scope requires downloading an alternate language runtime at install time or running a multi-hundred-KB obfuscated payload. The chain — install-time fetch of an alternate runtime specifically to execute an obfuscated sibling module that Node-oriented scanners will not evaluate — is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern, and it runs automatically on default `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
